title: Transport for Tourism
summary: Transport (from the Latin trans, 'across a port') is the movement of people or goods from one place to another. It links the tourist-generating area with the destination through a transit route, overcomes distance and decides the pace of tourist flow. The four modes are road, rail, air and water. In Mughal times Kos Minars measured distance, trees and wells were provided and sarais were built along the route. UNWTO recorded 1,184 million international travellers in 2015 (growth 4.4%).

Road: flexible, reliable, cheaper, accessible to many and can take the tourist to the final destination point; cars, taxis, coaches, buses and jeeps connect rail, air and water transport. Rail: the most suitable and cheap means for long distances, carries large numbers, has several coach classes (General, Sleeper, AC) and fast trains (Shatabdi, Rajdhani, Duranto). Water: the earliest type of boat was the raft; cruises, lakes, rivers, canals and backwaters offer water-based tourism; cheapest but slowest. Air: the fastest, second most popular mode globally after road, free from surface hindrances and a 'global village' maker, but costly.

National Highways (NHs) connect state capitals with main cities: about 2% of the road network but 40% of road-based traffic (23 NHs listed in the lesson). The first expressway is Mumbai–Pune; the Yamuna Expressway links Delhi with Agra (Taj Mahal). The Golden Quadrilateral links Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata and Chennai; the North-South corridor links Srinagar and Kanyakumari and the East-West corridor links Silchar and Porbandar (7,300 km). The Golden Triangle links Delhi, Agra and Jaipur (about 1,000 km); another links Puri, Konark and Bhubaneswar. State highways connect state capitals with districts; district and village roads promote rural tourism. Delhi is the 'city of flyovers'.

India has the second largest railway network in Asia and the fourth in the world (after the USA, Russia and China) and tops the world in passengers per kilometre. Tourism trains: Palace on Wheels (royal 7-day train for Rajasthan, Delhi and Agra), Fairy Queen (oldest steam locomotive; Delhi to Alwar and the Sariska tiger reserve), Heritage on Wheels (14 saloons connecting Bikaner, Gajner, Nawalgarh, Mandawa, Ramgarh and Shekhawati), Bharat Darshan (affordable package with accommodation, buses and guides), plus the Toy Train. The Darjeeling Himalayan Railway, Nilgiri Mountain Railway and Kalka-Shimla Railway are UNESCO World Heritage railways. The Delhi Metro is air-conditioned and links tourist sites; Kolkata's tram has run since British times.

About 97% of international tourists arrive in India by air; Delhi and Mumbai handle over 70%. Tourist charter flights can land at all designated international airports. India has about 7,500 km of coastline, 12 major ports and 185 non-major ports. West coast major ports: Kandla, Mumbai, Jawaharlal Nehru, Marmagao, Mangalore and Kochi; east coast: Tuticorin, Chennai, Visakhapatnam, Paradip, Haldia and Kolkata. Gujarat, Maharashtra and West Bengal have two major ports each (as stated in the lesson) and Tamil Nadu three. Inland waterways carry about 1% of traffic; the three National Waterways are Allahabad–Haldia (1,620 km), Sadiya–Dhubri (891 km) and Kottapuram–Kollam (205 km). Water tourism: Sunderbans, Goa cruises, rafting between Rishikesh and Haridwar, Dal Lake, Nainital and Chilika.

Clear information on location, distance and fares with timetables; updated arrival and departure information; good treatment for the aged and disabled; standard signs and symbols; better infrastructure and eco-friendly transport; clean terminals; action against cheats; and a tourist police, especially for women.

objective: Fill in the blanks. (a) The Yamuna Expressway connects ________ with the world-renowned site Taj Mahal in Agra. (b) The National Waterway running from Sadiya to ________ is 891 km long.
Answer in one or two words. (a) Which two cities are joined by the North-South corridor? (b) Which mode of transport has helped in promoting tourism?
(a) Srinagar and Kanyakumari. (b) Air transport (rail and road also help).
Fill in the blanks. (a) The earliest type of boat was the ________. (b) The ________ train has the oldest steam locomotive engine in India.
True or False. (a) Rail transport has transformed the whole world into a global village. (b) Road transport is a flexible and reliable means of transport.
(a) False: air transport has made the world a global village. (b) True.

Match Column A with Column B. A: (a) Palace on Wheels (b) Heritage on Wheels. B: (i) Bikaner, Gajner, Nawalgarh, Mandawa (ii) Seven-day royal train through Rajasthan, Delhi and Agra (iii) Oldest steam engine.
True or False. (a) National Highways are about 2% of the road network but carry 40% of road traffic. (b) About 97% of international tourists arrive in India by rail.
(a) True. (b) False: about 97% arrive by air.
Fill in the blanks. (a) India has the ________ largest railway network in the world. (b) The Golden Quadrilateral connects Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata and ________.
vsa: Explain any two characteristics of the Bharat Darshan special tourist train.

It is an affordable package that covers important tourist places of the country. The fare includes accommodation in the coaches, tourist buses for sightseeing, hall accommodation at night halts and guides.
April 2026
April 2025

or: Explain two advantages of rail transportation for tourists.
It is cheap and comfortable for long distances. A large number of people can travel together and the network reaches nearly all parts of the country.

vsa: Explain the relationship between transportation and tourism in two points.
Transport links the tourist-generating area with the destination, so tourism is impossible without it. Its capacity, speed, comfort and safety decide the pace of tourist flow.
October 2025
Mention any two measures to boost tourist transport.
Give clear information on location, distance, fares and timetables, and develop standard signs and symbols. Improve infrastructure, keep terminals clean and have a tourist police for help.
April 2025
Write two characteristics of air transport.
It is the fastest mode and saves time over thousands of kilometres. It is free from surface hindrances such as mountains and deserts and offers comfort and luxury.
Give two characteristics of road transport.
It is flexible, reliable and cheaper and can take the tourist up to the final destination. Vehicles such as cars, buses, taxis and jeeps connect rail, air and water transport.
Name any two tourism-promoting trains and state what each offers.
Palace on Wheels is a luxury seven-day royal train covering Rajasthan, Delhi and Agra. The Fairy Queen has the oldest steam engine and takes tourists to Alwar and Sariska.
What is the Golden Triangle? Why is it popular?
It is the route connecting Delhi, Agra and Jaipur, about 1,000 km long. It is popular because tourists visit the Taj Mahal at Agra and Jaipur and the desert areas around it.
Mention any two features of water transport for tourism in India.

It includes coastal shipping, inland waterways and sea transport, with cruises on rivers, lakes and backwaters. India has a 7,500 km coastline, 12 major ports and National Waterways such as Allahabad–Haldia.
sa: Describe any three characteristics of road transportation.

(i) It gives basic accessibility, connecting places and people with flexibility and reliability. (ii) It is cheaper and can take the tourist up to the final destination. (iii) Highways, flyovers and different vehicles (cars, coaches, buses) connect rail, air and water transport.
Explain the role of air transport in promoting tourism in India.

(i) It is the fastest mode, so tourists reach any place in the world within 24 hours. (ii) About 97% of international tourists arrive by air and Delhi and Mumbai handle over 70%; charter flights can land at 16 international airports. (iii) Airports are being modernised and airlines offer concessional tickets and packages for budget tourists.

or: Explain the role of rail transport in promoting tourism in India.

(i) The railways are cheap and comfortable for long distances and carry large numbers of domestic tourists. (ii) Tourist trains such as Palace on Wheels, Fairy Queen, Heritage on Wheels and Bharat Darshan promote tourism. (iii) UNESCO heritage rail lines, the Delhi Metro and Kolkata tram add tourist interest.

sa: Analyse the role of railways in tourism development in India.

(i) India has the fourth largest rail network and carries the most passengers per kilometre. (ii) Most domestic tourists depend on it for long journeys. (iii) Special tourist trains and heritage lines attract national and international tourists.
Explain the role of a tourist transport system in three points.

(i) It links tourist-generating areas with destinations. (ii) The capacity of the transport system decides the pace of tourist flow. (iii) Comfort, speed, safety, discounts and refreshments act as incentives and good or bad experiences stay in the tourist's mind.
Distinguish between air transport and water transport (three points).

(i) Air is the fastest; water is the slowest. (ii) Air is costly; water is the cheapest and carries heavy goods easily. (iii) Air transport covers long distances in hours and is free from surface hindrances; water transport gives cruise and boating experiences on rivers, lakes and the sea.
la: How is a road map important for tourists? Explain in six points.

(i) It shows the roads of an area and their condition in different seasons. (ii) It shows national, state and district highways and village roads in different ways. (iii) It shows petrol pumps, lodging and boarding facilities and places of public assistance. (iv) The distance matrix tells the distance between places, helping decide the journey and plan time. (v) It helps domestic tourists who travel by road choose routes. (vi) It helps reach destinations that rail and air do not directly serve.
How has air transport played an important role in the development of tourism in India? Explain in six points.

(i) It is the fastest mode and covers long distances in a few hours. (ii) About 97% of international tourists arrive by air. (iii) Delhi and Mumbai are the main entry points for over 70% of them. (iv) Charter flights can land at 16 designated international airports. (v) The government is upgrading airports for passenger comfort. (vi) Public and private airlines offer concessional tickets and special packages for lower-budget tourists.
Discuss the different means of tourist transport in India, in six points.

(i) Road: national and state highways, expressways and the Golden Quadrilateral and Triangle; flexible and reaches the destination. (ii) Rail: cheap for long distances with tourist trains such as Palace on Wheels and Bharat Darshan. (iii) Heritage railways, the metro and the tram add interest. (iv) Air: the fastest, carrying 97% of international arrivals. (v) Water: 12 major ports, inland waterways, cruises and rafting. (vi) The choice depends on geography, distance, time, comfort, safety and fares.
